title: Import command date defaults are fixed at process startup
reasoning: The default start and end dates are evaluated when add_arguments runs, not when handle executes. In a normal one-shot manage.py command this usually works, but it is incorrect if the command parser is reused in a long-lived process or test harness: a later invocation without explicit dates can import the stale date window from the first parser setup rather than the current day.
recommendation: Use None as the argparse default and compute date.today()-based defaults inside handle immediately before parsing or validating the date range.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for either management command, and this requires exercising repeated command invocations or parser reuse across a date boundary.
suggestedRegressionTest: Instantiate the command/parser with omitted dates while mocking the current date at execution time, then assert handle uses the mocked execution date rather than an earlier parser construction date.
minimumFixScope: Change both commands so --start_date and --end_date default to None and are filled in handle.
